summary.intent: Add Phase 27 (Writable Shares PoC) to the CipherBox roadmap and complete the full planning pipeline: discuss-phase, plan-phase (with research, UI-SPEC, and verification).
summary.outcome: Phase 27 was added to the roadmap, CONTEXT.md captured implementation decisions, RESEARCH.md and VALIDATION.md were generated, UI-SPEC.md passed checker after one revision cycle, and the planner was spawned — planning was in progress at the end of the session.

repo: CipherBox's server-relayed IPNS architecture sidesteps the 'unsolved multi-writer IPNS problem' entirely — all publishes go through the API which acts as the sequencing coordinator, so two writers on the same folder already work like two devices from the same user.

Vault-level IPNS keys (vault, vault-key-blob, byo-ipfs-config, device-registry) are HKDF-derived from the secp256k1 private key to enable self-sovereign recovery without parent metadata. Folder and file IPNS keys are randomly generated because their IPNS names are discoverable from parent folder metadata.

File IPNS keys were deliberately migrated from HKDF-derived to random in a pre-Phase 14 security review (`.planning/todos/done/2026-02-21-random-file-ipns-keys.md`) specifically to enable future write-sharing — deterministic derivation would have required sharing the user's master secp256k1 key.

Phase 14 explicitly deferred writable shares: read-write sharing requires giving recipients the IPNS private key, and the multi-writer problem was considered unsolved. Phase 27 revisits this with the server-coordination insight.
Milestone 4 TEAM-11 plans a proper cryptographic read/write key hierarchy (separate keys so viewers literally cannot write) — Phase 27 PoC is a stepping stone, not the final architecture.

The existing optimistic concurrency stack (expectedSequenceNumber + 409 retry + conflict banner + 30s polling) already handles multi-writer scenarios — no new conflict infrastructure needed for the PoC.

code.finding: Server-side expectedSequenceNumber check before every IPNS publish — the sequencing gate that makes multi-writer coordination work.
409 Conflict detection with automatic single-retry and re-sync on IPNS publish failure.
Subfolder IPNS keypair generation via generateEd25519Keypair() — random, not derived, enabling independent key sharing.
UI conflict banner with jitter-delayed retry for human-visible conflict resolution.
Sequence number comparison across network vs DB cache — highest wins, used for sync convergence.
File IPNS keypair generation via generateFileIpnsKeypair() — random after the 2026-02-21 migration from HKDF derivation.
Vault-level IPNS key derivation via HKDF — only the vault-discovery keys still use deterministic derivation.

workflow: The GSD add-phase tool generates slugs from the full description text, producing absurdly long directory names when the description is a paragraph rather than a short label. Manual rename required.
The plan-phase UI design contract gate (step 5.6) will halt planning if frontend indicators are detected and no UI-SPEC exists — must run /gsd:ui-phase first when this triggers.
The gsd-tools CLI auto-calculated depends-on as Phase 26 (previous phase) rather than Phase 14 (the actual logical predecessor) — manual ROADMAP.md edit was needed to correct it.
UI-SPEC checker enforced a 2-font-weight cap and 4px grid alignment, catching issues in the first draft and requiring a revision pass.

friction: Auto-generated phase slug from the long description was too long for a directory name — required manual rename of the phase directory and corresponding ROADMAP.md edits.
gsd-tools set depends-on to Phase 26 (sequential predecessor) rather than Phase 14 (semantic predecessor) — roadmap entry needed manual correction.
First /gsd:plan-phase 27 invocation was blocked by the UI design contract gate, requiring a detour through /gsd:ui-phase 27 before planning could proceed.
UI-SPEC required one revision cycle (typography and spacing fixes) before passing the 6-dimension checker.
open_items: Planning (PLAN.md files) was being generated by the planner agent at the end of the session — outcome unknown from the transcript.
Metadata-embedded sharing (hiding the social graph from the server) deferred — would require embedding share records in encrypted folder metadata rather than server-side shares table.
Attribution and audit trail for write actions deferred — Phase 27 PoC treats multi-writer edits identically to multi-device sync with no per-user attribution.
Transitive re-sharing explicitly prohibited for PoC — owners can upgrade/downgrade permissions but recipients cannot re-share.
Milestone 4 TEAM-11 proper cryptographic read/write key hierarchy (separate keys enforcing viewer cannot-write at crypto layer) is a separate future phase from this PoC.
